title: Algorithm Analysis and Design
blurb: Everything for the endsem on 26 Nov: divide and conquer, FFT, graphs, stable and maximum matchings, Hall's theorem, greedy and Huffman, dynamic programming, max flow, randomized algorithms and fingerprinting, NP-hardness. Built from Lectures 1 to 24, the tutorials including NP, both assignments, the midsem, both quizzes and both class tests, with every exam problem solved against the official rubric.

docs.title: Start here: the endsem map
docs.about: Syllabus, how the papers are marked, which lecture each exam question came from, and a plan for the last day

docs.title: Lectures 1 to 3: numbers, divide and conquer, lower bounds
docs.about: Peasant multiplication, Euclid, recursion trees, the master theorem, merge sort, Karatsuba, Strassen, the sorting lower bound, Hadamard transforms

docs.title: Lectures 3, 4 and 8: polynomials and the FFT
docs.about: Coefficient and value representations, roots of unity, the FFT recursion, the Fourier matrix and its inverse, polynomial multiplication, a polynomial from its roots

docs.title: Lectures 4 and 5: graphs, shortest paths, MSTs
docs.about: DFS and edge types, DAGs and topological order, SCCs, BFS, Dijkstra, Bellman–Ford, DAG shortest paths, cut property, Kruskal with union–find, Prim, MST uniqueness

docs.title: Lectures 6 to 9: stable matchings, Hall, maximum matchings
docs.about: Gale–Shapley and its proofs, proposer-optimality, Hall's theorem, SDRs, Latin squares, regular bipartite graphs, augmenting paths, Berge, Kuhn, König

docs.title: Lecture 10: greedy algorithms and Huffman codes
docs.about: Exchange arguments, prefix-free codes and trees, Huffman's algorithm and its proof, Kraft's inequality, k-ary Huffman, interval scheduling and interval partitioning

docs.title: Lectures 11 to 13: dynamic programming
docs.about: The five-step DP recipe, weighted interval scheduling, DAG paths, LIS in O(n log n), knapsack, sequence alignment, cloth cutting, pebbling, trees, and the assignment problems

docs.title: Lectures 14 to 18: max flow and min cut
docs.about: Flows, cuts, weak duality, residual graphs, Ford–Fulkerson, max-flow min-cut, integrality, Edmonds–Karp, and every reduction the course uses

docs.title: Lectures 19 to 21: randomized algorithms and fingerprinting
docs.about: Linearity of expectation, random MaxCut, the probabilistic method, Schwartz–Zippel, equality testing, Rabin–Karp, streaming palindromes, 2D Rabin–Karp

docs.title: Lecture 22 and the NP tutorial: reductions and NP-hardness
docs.about: Balanced brackets, streaming lower bounds, P and NP with the verifier template, the direction check, Cook–Levin, ETH, XOR-SAT, and Max-Cut is NP-hard via NAE-3SAT, plus the classic chain with proofs

docs.title: Midsem, fully solved
docs.about: All five midsem problems with the official rubric: Karatsuba, FFT, Gale–Shapley, Huffman, room assignment, SDRs and Latin squares, the battery DP

docs.title: Quizzes I and II and Class Tests I and II, fully solved
docs.about: Domino tiling via Hall, peasant multiplication, Hadamard in O(n log n), random acyclic subgraphs, matching as flow, Hall via max-flow min-cut, Edmonds–Karp trace, vertex capacities, Menger, streaming palindrome check, 2D Rabin–Karp

docs.title: Practice problems and assignments, solved
docs.about: The Moodle practice set, magic squares and König, both assignments, and new endsem-style problems on every topic

docs.title: Last-hour cheat sheet
docs.about: Every algorithm, running time, theorem and proof skeleton on a few pages
